transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-01
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Khatri (Redwood SE), Martin Cole (ScoutWave CTO), Aisha Rahman (Head of ML), Jon Park (Platform), Lina Gómez (SRE), Benji (Ops)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Agree POC scope: 2 week replay benchmark then pilot. Success criteria around P95/P99 latency and per-1k token cost. Data/security: VPC + KMS review.

Topics: workload shape, QPS burst patterns, concurrency, token length distributions, benchmark harness, timeline, responsibilities.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samantha (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros before we jump in
[00:12] Martin (ScoutWave): Sure, I'm Martin, CTO. We run a conversational checkout flow and want to move inference off our prototype infra into a production runner, looking at both hosted and dedicated options
[00:22] Samantha: Great. Diego, Priya — you two will drive the benchmark design and throughput modeling with them
[00:27] Diego (Redwood SE): Yep, hi all. Quick note — we'll lean on a replay harness but also synth bursts to capture tail behavior
[00:35] Aisha (ScoutWave): Our immediate need: sub-350ms P95 on normal traffic and P99 under 800ms for checkout requests. Cost target is roughly $0.40 per 1k tokens across typical conversation lengths — we can be flexible if latency improves
[00:50] Priya: Okay that's helpful. Can you tell us current baseline QPS and what peak bursts look like?
[00:57] Martin: Baseline usually around 90–120 QPS globally, but there are marketing-driven blasts where we see up to 550 QPS for short 3–8 minute windows. Concurrency tends to sit around 300 active sessions, spikes to 700 during checkout promos
[01:15] Jon (Platform): To add, our average session is 4 requests per conversation, but the output token length varies a lot — some responses are 40 tokens, others 400 tokens for full summaries. Input tokens typically 20–60. We can provide logs
[01:33] Diego: That distribution matters a lot for setting batch sizes and liveness. If outputs skew heavy we need to capture that for KV cache pressure and memory footprint
[01:43] Martin: Yep, we're seeing a fat tail — about 5% of responses > 250 tokens
[01:49] Samantha: Perfect. Aisha, will you be able to share anonymized message logs or token histograms?
[01:55] Aisha: Yes. We'll scrub PII and provide a histogram plus a small sample of raw messages by end of week
[02:03] Samantha: Great. On success criteria — besides latency and cost, what else would you gate on? Error rate? Quality regressions?
[02:10] Aisha: Error rate under 0.1% and no regressions on two evaluation prompts we have. We'll provide the eval set
[02:18] Diego: We'll run those evals pre/post to check for any output quality shifts when using quantized or smaller model variants
[02:25] Martin: Also need to know the behavior if we hit capacity — can we failover to a higher-latency but cheaper model or route to a different region?
[02:35] Priya: Yes, Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible variants. We'll include that in the playbook
[02:42] Jon: On security — we require VPC peering for Dedicated or a private deployment. SOC2 is a must, and key management must integrate with our KMS/HSM
[02:52] Samantha: Understood. We'll attach SOC2 and our security whitepaper; for KMS we support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations in private deployments
[03:02] Lina: Also audit logs — retention and token redaction matter for us
[03:08] Diego: We'll log token-level events at the request metadata level but we don't persist raw prompt text unless configured. We can redact or hash tokens per your policy
[03:17] Benji: Slight side question, what about batching? If we set aggressive batching for cost, can we still meet latency?
[03:25] Priya: That's the tradeoff. We'll run a parameter sweep: batch size vs max latency SLO. In many cases prefix caching and KV reuse lets you keep latency tight while increasing throughput
[03:35] Samantha: For the POC we suggest two runs: a baseline 48h replay at your real QPS shape, and a focused 24h stress window with synthetic bursts to 2x observed peaks to test autoscaling and tail behavior
[03:48] Martin: Sounds reasonable. We want the replay to mimic the exact temporal pattern — hour-of-day and marketing pulses
[03:55] Diego: We'll ask for a week of traffic to extract daily patterns, but you can give us a representative 48h slice if that's easier
[04:03] Aisha: We'll provide a 7-day aggregated histogram and call out the pulse times so you can synthesize the bursts
[04:11] Samantha: Timeline-wise we propose: receive logs by 2027-06-04, Redwood runs initial analysis and synthetic config by 2027-06-07, replay runs starting 2027-06-10 for 48h, then tuning and a results review on 2027-06-14. Decision to pilot by 2027-06-16
[04:29] Martin: That's tight but doable. What's included in the POC vs pilot?
[04:34] Samantha: POC = sizing and benchmark only (no SLA). Pilot = 4-week production-like run on Dedicated or private infra with limited seats and an SLA window for latency and uptime
[04:44] Jon: Could you outline the Dedicated delta vs Hosted costs? We need numbers to decide if private infra is needed
[04:51] Samantha: I'll send a detailed cost table. Short summary: Hosted is quickest to start, Dedicated gives capacity isolation and more predictable unit cost at higher commits. Private adds network control and KMS but includes additional ops/flat fee
[05:03] Aisha: For benchmarking, does Redwood need any model artifacts or will you use our selected model from your catalog?
[05:10] Diego: We'll test with the model you plan to use. If you have a custom fine-tuned checkpoint we'll need a secure transfer path or we can pull from your private registry in a VPC setup
[05:20] Martin: We're planning to use the open LLM 'Harbor-3B-Chat' tuned in-house — we can either share the weights via a private S3 and presigned URL or let you pull from our ECR-like registry
[05:31] Priya: Both work. For the POC, a model pull into an ephemeral testing environment is fine. For pilot we'd want the private deployment to access it directly behind your registry
[05:40] Benji: Any constraints on GPU types? We currently use A100s in our infra but not sure if Redwood has preference
[05:46] Diego: Redwood's runtime supports a variety of GPUs; for this model 80-bit or 8-bit quantization paths prefer A100 or H100-class runtime. We'll recommend a profile after we see token histograms
[05:58] Samantha: Aisha, can you confirm the percent of long responses? You mentioned 5% >250 tokens earlier
[06:05] Aisha: Correct. Median output is ~120, mean is 150, 95th is about 280, 99th around 520 but that's rare
[06:14] Diego: That 99th is important for memory and KV cache sizing. We'll simulate those tails in the stress run
[06:20] Martin: How do you measure cost? Per token or per request?
[06:24] Samantha: For hosted it's per token with a small request overhead. For Dedicated we price reserved capacity (committed GPU hours) + a marginal token charge in some configs. We'll give the full breakdown
[06:35] Jon: For the benchmark harness, do you provide a replay tool or should we prepare our own traces?
[06:41] Priya: We have a replay tool that accepts ndjson request hints and a token histogram. If you can provide session boundaries and timestamps we'll replay them with fidelity
[06:50] Martin: We'll provide session-based logs. Expect some noise — could be incomplete messages or system prompts attached
[06:56] Diego: No problem, the replay can tolerate partials. We'll log mismatches in the post-run report
[07:02] Samantha: Let's talk success gating. Proposed criteria: P95 < 350ms, P99 < 800ms, error rate < 0.1%, quality pass on provided eval set, and unit cost below your target range or within acceptable tradeoff
[07:16] Aisha: We accept a 10% cost increase if latency improves by 20% on P95/P99
[07:23] Priya: We'll include a sensitivity table: latency vs batch size vs quantization level vs cost
[07:30] Martin: How do you handle model fallbacks during overloads? Do you have automatic variant routing?
[07:36] Diego: Yes, smart routing with policy-based fallbacks. We can route by latency budget, region, or customer tier. For POC we'll leave a canary fallback for the stress run
[07:45] Jon: Any network prep we need? Will you open inbound peering requests?
[07:50] Samantha: For Dedicated/VPC we'll start a peering ticket. For hosted we just need IP allowlists and possibly egress configs for registry pull
[07:58] Lina: On logging — do you keep raw prompts on Redwood? We have strict data residency rules
[08:04] Diego: We recommend redaction by default; we can keep token counts and metadata for troubleshooting. For pilot, if you're on Private, you can opt to never leave your VPC and controls remain with you
[08:15] Martin: Great. Aisha will send the logs. What about benchmark metrics — what will you return in the report?
[08:21] Priya: We'll provide per-endpoint QPS, concurrency, per-token latency distribution (P50/P90/P95/P99/P99.9), throughput, GPU utilization, batch size distribution, memory footprints, error types, and a cost model extrapolated to monthly usage
[08:36] Samantha: We'll also include tuning recommendations: cache TTLs, batch limits, quantization level suggestions, routing policy suggestions
[08:44] Benji: For the 48h replay, can we get an interim check after 12h? We want to catch misconfig early
[08:49] Diego: Yes, we do a rolling health dashboard and will flag any runaway errors or tail latency within the first 6–12 hours
[08:58] Samantha: Okay, to recap: Aisha sends anonymized logs by 6/4, Redwood drafts harness by 6/7, replay 6/10–6/12, review 6/14, decision 6/16. Action owners documented in the notes
[09:12] Martin: Perfect. Anything else?
[09:16] Jon: One last thing — during the POC will you support custom metrics exports to our Datadog?
[09:21] Priya: Yes, we can stream metrics via an output plugin during the replay and pilot. We'll coordinate the metric names and tags
[09:29] Aisha: Good. Also please confirm that your runtime won't log raw customer prompts in S3 — we need confirmation in writing
[09:36] Samantha: We'll include that in the security pack: default redaction and an explicit config for logs. We'll send the SOC2 + security whitepaper after the call
[09:44] Martin: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up on the logs and the registry access for the model
[09:49] Samantha: Thanks all. We'll share the next steps and a calendar invite for the replay start.
[09:54] (call ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional speaker mislabels and filler words were present in the live transcription. Proper nouns like 'Harbor-3B-Chat' may be auto-corrected in places.
